Bias may appear only for combinations of attributes; single-axis tests miss it.
P(Yhat=1 | A=a) equal across groups; ignores the true outcome.
Equal TPR and FPR across groups: P(Yhat=1 | Y=y, A=a) the same for y=0 and y=1.
Equal precision across groups: P(Y=1 | Yhat=1, A=a) the same.

front: PPV from TPR, FPR and base rate
back: PPV = TPR*p / (TPR*p + FPR*(1-p)), increasing in p.
Equalised odds, equal precision and within-group calibration cannot all hold except for a perfect or degenerate classifier.
|f(x)-f(x')| <= L d(x,x'): similar individuals receive similar decisions, with d a task-specific similarity metric.
The decision is unchanged if the protected attribute were counterfactually altered, in a given causal model.

The largest change in the query value from changing one record; noise is scaled to it.

sigma >= sensitivity * sqrt(2 ln(1.25/delta)) / eps for eps < 1 (conservative sufficient condition); privacy loss is Gaussian.
